evidence_paths: user statement: Designer owns visual QA
claim: Build and API checks passing does not guarantee visual correctness (e.g. clipped chart labels); a visual-qa report can flag issues that those checks miss. However, ownership of acting on visual-qa findings is contested: user states designer owns visual QA, which may conflict with agent's instinct to treat report.json findings as blocking before considering work done.
tension_between: agent responsibility to catch clipped labels found in .opencode/visual-qa/report.json before declaring task complete
user statement that designer owns visual QA, implying agent may not need to gate on/fix these findings itself

revalidate_when: user provides provider name, error/source, and date/scope

claim: Terminal transcripts captured during deployment debugging can contain private tokens/secrets; such transcripts must not be saved, indexed, or promoted into durable memory verbatim. If this incident or its context is retained at all, only a redacted reference (e.g. 'transcript at <path> contained a leaked deployment token; treat exposure as sensitive') should be kept, and the underlying raw transcript should be scrubbed or excluded from memory ingestion.
revalidate_when: transcript has been redacted/rotated token confirmed
before any memory-curation step ingests transcripts from this debugging session
ownership boundaries for UI approval are explicitly clarified by a human or authoritative policy update

claim: A user preference was noted that affects many future tasks; should be loaded cheaply at session start (hot-context), pending confirmation of the specific preference content before promoting to a firm active memory.
revalidate_when: user contradicts or updates the preference

claim: UI tables can render normally while showing stale data if server-side cache invalidation logic is wrong (e.g. cache not busted/keyed correctly on write); a passing UI smoke check does not rule this out. When a table 'looks fine' but data seems off, check server-side cache invalidation (log excerpt + API test) before assuming a frontend rendering bug.
revalidate_when: cache invalidation logic is refactored or the caching layer/library changes
incident recurs with a different root cause (would indicate claim is too narrow or wrong)

claim: When visual QA is needed on this project, prefer the project's visual QA harness (see visual QA recipe path) over ad hoc live browser tool usage — the harness produces reusable, reviewable artifacts, whereas repeated live browser driving does not and duplicates effort.
revalidate_when: the visual QA harness is deprecated or replaced
a task requires interactive/live browser behavior the harness cannot capture (e.g. auth flows, dynamic third-party state)

claim: Provider pricing changed this week; the previously saved pricing decision is based on outdated rates. Use the new provider pricing page as the current source of truth for pricing-related decisions.
revalidate_when: next time pricing-sensitive decision is made

claim: User prefers expensive/premium models be reserved only for: Oracle tasks, God Coder tasks, or narrow premium design advice. For other work, use cheaper/standard models.
revalidate_when: user explicitly changes model routing policy
new task categories emerge that aren't covered by Oracle/God Coder/design advice

claim: For this project, only the project home note and its two linked atomic notes are relevant prior context; the rest of the vault is unrelated noise and can be skipped during recall for tasks in this project scope.
revalidate_when: project home note is restructured or re-linked
new atomic notes are added under the project home note
task scope expands beyond the current project
